content:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT host/queue: hosted-api.p99_latency > 30s for 2m, queue_depth=18,400, GPU_pool_util=99%. Incident key HOSTED-QUEUE-EXHAUSTION. Paging ops-oncall. Links: https://ops.metrics/redwood/hosted-queue
Jordan: acked. I'm on it — standing up an ops bridge. @ops-oncall you own mitigation.
ops-oncall: oncall here. seeing a steady backlog growth after a traffic spike at 14:18 UTC. Autoscaler attempted to create nodes but provisioner shows heartbeat timeouts. Suspect provisioner -> cloud API throttling + thin pool exhaustion.
Michael: looking at provisioner logs now. saw repeated:
```
E 14:19:03 provisioner leader: heartbeat timeout to cloud-api (429)
W 14:19:10 provisioner: pending node create stuck state=waiting_for_quota
```
We attempted scale x3 but the API returned rate-limited responses.
Diana: customer impact: p95 jumped 4.8s -> 12.3s, p99 ~30s, 8 active customers seeing timeouts. Error rate for generate calls +10%. Backlog per-shard top: shard-us-west-1=9.1k, shard-us-east-1=7.0k.
Alice: applied an emergency token-level ingress throttle for new sessions to reduce steady-state inflow. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/ingress/rate-limit -d '{"policy":"token","limit_per_min":4000}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
```
Alice: also flipped on short-lived 2s prefix cache for common system prompts to reduce token work.
Sam: starting manual provisioning in the cloud as a short-term bypass of the provisioner. running:
```
cloudctl compute instances create --pool gpu-dedicated --count 6 --type a100-40g --labels "tmp-surge"
```
Michael: I restarted the provisioner leader pod to re-elect and flush heartbeat backoffs:
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/provisioner
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/provisioner --tail=200 | tail -n 40
```
snippet from logs:
```
I 14:24:22 provisioner: leader elected id=prov-3
I 14:24:25 provisioner: new node pool attach accepted, nodes=6
```
ops-oncall: after restart we're seeing partial node joins, but one thin-provision pool hit allocation limit and OOM-guard triggered evictions for low-priority tenants. Evictions saved capacity but caused some 503s for low-priority customers.
Jordan: routing change: enabling model-fallback policy for hosted-api: when queue_depth>5k route non-SLA tenants to smaller-quantized model. Applied config:
```
routes.hosted-api.fallback = [{"priority":"low","model":"redwood/opt-3b-q4","condition":"queue>5000"}]
```
Michael: manual nodes from cloudctl are joining the cluster now, autoscaler metrics show available GPUs rising +6. Provisioner heartbeats stabilized after leader restart and backoff reset.
incident-bot: UPDATE: backlog trend reversed (growth -> plateau) at 14:28 UTC. New_nodes_joined=6. p95 decreased to ~6.5s, p99 to ~14s. Queue_depth=10.2k.
Diana: contacting top affected customers with ETA for mitigation and note on degraded throughput. No PII exposed. Support ticket numbers created for the top 3 customers.
Alice: rolled back the most aggressive rate-limits for tokens affected by customer complaints, kept new-session throttle in place. Observing CPU/GPU utilization.
ops-oncall: monitoring for 30m. recommend follow-ups: (1) increase provisioner cloud API rate window, (2) raise thin-pool allocation cap for surge windows, (3) postmortem to cover autoscaler backoff behaviour.
Jordan: handing off to night oncall @sam. Summary: provisioner heartbeat/timeouts caused autoscaler to stall under a traffic spike; manual nodes + provisioner restart recovered capacity; temporary rate-limits + model-fallback reduced pressure. Watch p99 and eviction logs.
Sam: acked. I'll take over and run the follow-up checklist. Paging steps noted in bridge. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: NOTE: bridge created https://zoom/ops/bridges/hosted-queue-1767777777, severity=sev2, runbook=hosted-queue-autoscale. Marked incident state=mitigated at 14:31 UTC.
Jordan: adding final notes — no SLA breach yet for paid customers, some low-priority tenants experienced 503s from eviction policy. Will open a postmortem and action items for provisioner rate limits and autoscaler exponential backoff tuning.
Sam: will escalate quota with cloud provider if we see similar patterns tomorrow. closing active page handoff.
